segments.speaker: Participant
segments.segment_type: initial evidence selection and review allocation
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The committee centered its first working session on Curriculum B after hearing the neighboring district's enthusiasm, while A and C received only checklist-level review.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The committee allocated shortlisting attention toward B based on another district's enthusiasm rather than independent review.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: During later scoring, Curriculum A was framed as needing to be good enough to change minds about B rather than evaluated independently.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Curriculum B had become an implicit reference point against which the subsequently reviewed Curriculum A was judged.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The participant vividly remembered a concrete classroom success story but retained little of the less memorable multi-school statistical report.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The vivid anecdote was more mentally available and consequently more influential than the statistical evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Testimonials confirming the committee's favorable view of B received little scrutiny, while the potentially disconfirming statistical report was deferred.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The committee accepted confirmatory evidence readily and deprioritized evidence that could complicate its existing preference.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The pilot teacher's pacing concern was acknowledged but not investigated, and a committee member privately withheld reservations because of the room's atmosphere.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Consensus pressure and a pre-existing majority preference suppressed full airing and investigation of dissent.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The chair averaged widely divergent scores for Curriculum A into one composite without investigating why the ratings differed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The mean was treated as a settled summary despite masking disagreement caused by different levels of review.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: No candidates were emitted, so this threshold is identical to all identified confidence levels.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: No change because the RAG emitted no candidates.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At high_and_moderate, 4 of 6 positive segments were detected with no false alarms; the Bandwagon and low-confidence Averaging segments were missed at this recommended threshold.

overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate the result is the same; including low-confidence findings recovers the Averaging mechanism, yielding 5 of 6 true positives and F1 0.9091.

main_failure_modes: The Bandwagon effect was not identified as a separate occurrence from Anchoring.
The averaging mechanism was left without a bias label, producing a strict label-resolution error at low confidence.
main_strengths: Groupthink, Availability/availability heuristic, Anchoring, and Confirmation were correctly localized with full mechanisms.
Interview quotations were valid and evidence-faithful.
The RAG accurately disclosed that retrieved corpus support was unavailable.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong precision and good mechanism coverage once moderate confidence is included, but it underdetects the externally driven Bandwagon instance and exposes a taxonomy-resolution gap for the low-confidence averaging mechanism.
